subject: Commitment structure — ramp timing & prepay options
messages:
From: Jordan Ellis <jordan.ellis@stratifyai.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.ai>
Cc: Taylor Nguyen <taylor.nguyen@stratifyai.com>
Date: 2026-05-17T16:12:00Z
Subject: Initial ask — commit sizing + prepay structure

Hi Ava,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — StratifyAI is excited about Redwood's performance profile. We're trying to put together a procurement request for a Dedicated deployment and I wanted to get clarity on two things so we can model TCO: 1) the recommended phased ramp (GPUs and TPMs) that you typically see for customers of our size, and 2) how discounting behaves if we prepay annually vs. a 2-year upfront prepay.

Current thinking (internal): we expect to move from a pilot (8 A100-equivalent GPUs) to production with peak steady-state of ~80 GPUs and 150 TPM within 18 months. Budget owners prefer an annual prepay cadence but the CFO is open to a multi-year upfront if the economics are compelling.

Can you:
- Share a sample ramp cadence you would recommend (month-by-month or quarter-by-quarter) for the 18-month window
- Provide a few pricing scenarios: (A) annual prepay with year-by-year billing, (B) 2-year upfront prepay, including effective % discount and any credits for unused capacity or conversion to hosted usage
- Confirm whether SLA/credits differ by prepay option and whether there's an escrow clause for capacity guarantees

Attachment: StratifyAI_RFP_SS.docx (procurement questions)

Appreciate a quick sketch — we're aiming to present options at exec review next Tues.

Best,
Jordan
Head of Infrastructure
StratifyAI
From: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Ellis <jordan.ellis@stratifyai.com>
Cc: Taylor Nguyen <taylor.nguyen@stratifyai.com>, Kim Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-18T02:08:00Z
Subject: Re: Initial ask — commit sizing + prepay structure

Jordan — thanks, glad the demo was useful. Below is a pragmatic two-track proposal (high level) and an attached sample Statement of Commitment + ramp calculator to run scenarios. I've kept the options comparable so you can show the CFO the tradeoffs.

Summary (quick):
- Target window: 18 months pilot->steady state (matches your ask)
- Option A — Annual prepay (renew each year): lower upfront cash, competitive discounts, annual true-up.
  - Year 1: commit 18 GPUs average (pilot + staged rollout), Year 2: 56 GPUs, Year 3: 80 GPUs steady state (we model as Q1/Q2 ramp into Year 2).
  - Discount: 15% off list for annual prepay (billed at the start of each year).
  - Conversion: unused prepay converts to platform credit usable for hosted API or future Dedicated invoices within 12 months.
  - SLA: standard Dedicated SLA (99.9% uptime) with monthly credits for missed SLO.

- Option B — 2-year upfront prepay (single payment at signing): higher discount, committed capacity reserve.
  - Modeled commit: Year 1 (18 GPUs average), Year 2 (72 GPUs average) — weighted to match your 18-month timing.
  - Discount: 22% off list across the full two-year commitment.
  - Conversion: unused capacity can be reallocated as credits or applied to burst capacity; early termination triggers a 90-day unwind with pro-rata refund minus a setup fee.
  - SLA & escrow: we can add an escrow-style capacity guarantee for core reserved pool; terms will include a capped refund schedule if we fail to provision reserved capacity.

Flexible ramp triggers (recommended):
- Usage-triggered tranche: if your utilization of committed pool exceeds 75% for two consecutive months, next tranche is a 30-day notice and auto-provision.
- Milestone-trigger: provide a calendar-based ramp tied to feature launch dates (we can mark in the SoC).

Other commercial levers:
- Prepay mix: we can structure a blended payment (e.g., 60% upfront, 40% annualized) to achieve intermediate economics.
- Quantization/TPM profile: pricing for TPM (throughput-multiplier) is layered; we'll include a TPM credit schedule in the spreadsheet.

I've attached: SRAT_Statement_of_Commitment_v1.pdf and ramp-schedule-calc.xlsx — the calc shows per-month GPU-hour equivalencies and effective blended $/GPU-hour for each option.

Next steps: tell me which option the CFO prefers (annual vs upfront) and any mandatory procurement constraints (escrow, PO cadence, required audit evidence). Happy to hop on a 30-min pricing call this week.

Thanks,
Ava Chen
Senior Account Executive — Redwood Inference
ava_chen@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0192
Attachment: SRAT_Statement_of_Commitment_v1.pdf (PDF), ramp-schedule-calc.xlsx (Excel)
From: Taylor Nguyen <taylor.nguyen@stratifyai.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jordan Ellis <jordan.ellis@stratifyai.com>
Date: 2026-05-18T20:36:00Z
Subject: Re: Initial ask — commit sizing + prepay structure

Ava — thanks for the clear breakdown, that helps. A few follow-ups from procurement/CFO:

1) Can you convert the 22% two-year upfront discount into an equivalent effective $/GPU-hour assuming our expected utilization profile? The attached spreadsheet looked good but we need a single blended number for execs.
2) Our CFO is asking whether unused prepay credits that convert to hosted API credits can be transferred to another BU or used to offset overages beyond the committed pool.
3) SOC 2 + data residency: we will need SOC 2 Type II report and confirmation that logs/keys are retained in US regions only.  
4) Escrow: procurement prefers an escrow clause or capacity-backed SLA with explicit refund caps — would Redwood accept a 1.5x capacity credit (capped) if failure to provision reserved pool occurs for >30 days?

We're leaning toward a blended prepay (roughly 60% upfront at signing, remainder annual) if it buys us better economics and a flexible unwind. Can you provide the blended pricing and confirm the SOC2/region details?

Attachment: StratifyAI_RFP_SS.docx (procurement checklist)

—Taylor
Head of Procurement
StratifyAI
From: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.ai>

Date: 2026-05-19T03:15:00Z
Subject: Internal: quick approval request — concession for StratifyAI (STRAT-2026-01)

Team — looping you in on the StratifyAI negotiation. Highlights: their preferred model is blended prepay (60% upfront / 40% annual) with an ask for a stronger upfront discount and an aggressive escrow capacity credit (1.5x for >30-day failure).

My proposed counter (to close):
- Convert the 22% two-year upfront to a blended schedule: 18% effective discount when structured 60% upfront + 40% annual (we keep list pricing on annual band for Year 2, apply an upfront credit to reach 18% blended).
- Accept a limited escrow-style capacity credit: 1.25x capped credit if we miss provisioning >30 days (we should not accept 1.5x).
- Offer a one-time onboarding credit equal to 5% of Year 1 prepay to help their CFO with capital smoothing.
- Add a 90-day unwind schedule for early termination with pro-rata refund less onboarding credit and setup fee.

Asks: Ben — okay to approve the 18% blended concession and the onboarding credit? Kim — confirm SOC 2 + region confirmation language we can share. Lauren — please prepare a short addendum (ramp-flex-addendum.pdf) describing the usage-triggered tranche and the 75% utilization rule.

Need to reply to Taylor by EOD tomorrow to hit their exec review.

Thanks,
Ava

Jordan / Taylor — thanks for the detailed list. Per internal approvals, here's our counter and a proposed path to sign: 

Key commercial (blended prepay):
- Structure: 60% upfront at signing, 40% billed at start of Year 2 (annual). Total commitment covers two years of reserved pool.
- Effective discount: 18% blended vs list when combined with a one-time onboarding credit equal to 5% of Year 1 prepay.
- Unused prepay credits: transferable across StratifyAI BUs and can be applied to hosted API overages or future Dedicated invoices (valid for 12 months).
- Escrow/capacity credit: we can accept an escrow-style capacity guarantee with a capped credit of 1.25x the affected tranche if Redwood fails to provision reserved capacity for >30 days.
- SLA: Dedicated SLA remains standard; we will provide SOC 2 Type II report and confirm logs/keys stay in US regions for this tenancy (will deliver redacted SOC 2 attestation).
- Termination: 90-day unwind with pro-rata refund less onboarding credit and setup fees.

Operational/technical:
- Lauren attached a short addendum describing the usage-triggered tranche (ramp-flex-addendum.pdf) and the 75% utilization auto-provision rule.
- Attached is an updated ramp-schedule-calc.xlsx with a single blended $/GPU-hour number for your exec pack.

DocuSign: I've included the DocuSign link to a draft SoC with these points: https://www.docusign.net/1234ABCD (placeholder). If this aligns, I'll finalize and route for signature.
